qualifying_updates.date_basis: Visible publication date on source page.
qualifying_updates.summary: OpenAI described GPT-Red, an internal automated red-teaming model trained through self-play to generate prompt-injection attacks and improve robustness of production models. The post highlights third-party data surfaces such as browsers, connected apps, local files, tool outputs, and code repositories as realistic injection locations.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local agent workflows should treat prompt-injection testing as a repeatable harness capability, not only a manual security exercise. Coding-agent evals should include tool-output, repository, browser, email, and local-file injection scenarios, with human review retained for attack classes automated red-teamers may miss.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Add or update downstream guidance around adversarial prompt-injection harnesses, indirect-injection test cases, and prompt-injection evidence required before trusting agent tool use.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Improvements to secret scanning and public monitoring
qualifying_updates.date_basis: Visible publication date on changelog page.
qualifying_updates.summary: GitHub announced secret scanning improvements, including new detector support, push protection defaults for VolcEngine secrets, a `secret_category` webhook field, and public monitoring insight cards that break down leaks by attribution, member counts, and verified domains.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: AI-assisted development workflows need secret-leak triage that can distinguish provider-specific and generic or AI-detected secrets, route webhook payloads correctly, and connect public exposure back to enterprise membership or domain attribution.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Keep local guidance focused on secret-handling workflow: alert categorization, webhook routing, public-monitoring exposure evidence, and package or agent outputs that may introduce credentials.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Advanced search for Projects is generally available
qualifying_updates.date_basis: URL slug and visible changelog placement show July 16, 2026; page content is a GitHub changelog post.
qualifying_updates.summary: GitHub Projects views added advanced `AND` and `OR` search and a `reviews:` filter for pull request items backed by reviewer-state fields.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Agentic engineering boards can encode review state, queue hygiene, and agent-human handoff status in project filters rather than maintaining separate manual views. This is useful for source workflows that track AI-authored pull requests, review gates, and unresolved review ownership.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Consider adding source-workflow guidance for project filters that separate AI-generated PRs by review state, human owner, and deployment or merge readiness.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Runtime Security for Third-Party GitHub Actions Runners: Bitrise, Blacksmith, Depot, Namespace, and Warp
qualifying_updates.date_basis: Visible publication date on source page.
qualifying_updates.summary: StepSecurity described Harden-Runner support for third-party GitHub Actions runner providers and emphasized that runner changes do not change the supply-chain threat model for jobs that install dependencies and hold deployment or signing secrets.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Coding-agent and CI harness guidance should treat third-party runners as equivalent-risk execution surfaces. Runtime monitoring, step attribution, egress policy, and dashboard evidence should follow the workload across hosted and third-party runner providers.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Update local practice only if needed around runner-neutral evidence: every agent-run CI job should have event attribution, outbound-network visibility, and policy controls regardless of runner provider.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Harden-Runner Block Mode Now Available for macOS and Windows GitHub-Hosted Runners
qualifying_updates.date_basis: Visible publication date on source page.
qualifying_updates.summary: StepSecurity announced Harden-Runner v2.20.0 block-mode support for macOS and Windows GitHub-hosted runners, moving those environments from outbound-traffic visibility to egress enforcement.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: AI-assisted package installation and generated build scripts can run on macOS and Windows jobs that hold signing certificates, provisioning profiles, and API keys. Agent-governed CI needs OS-neutral egress policy, not Linux-only enforcement.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Agent workflows that let tools install dependencies or run generated scripts should include egress-baseline review and block-mode promotion steps for every runner OS used in the delivery path.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Coding Agents 2.0: Interface, Inference, and Verification
qualifying_updates.date_basis: Visible publication date on source page.
qualifying_updates.summary: Gradient published a coding-agent stack map that separates interface, inference, orchestration, fleets, open coding agents, and verification layers. The post frames coding fleets as parallel agent execution where human attention becomes the scarce resource.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local wiki can use this as a practice signal for separating agent orchestration from verification capacity. Multi-agent fan-out should be paired with review budgets, verification queues, and explicit acceptance gates rather than only more agent parallelism.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Potential ingest target is multi-agent coordination and verification-tax guidance: every fleet pattern needs owner assignment, merge conflict control, review capacity, and stop conditions.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Atlassian Extends AI Reach of Jira Into Agentic Engineering Workflows
qualifying_updates.date_basis: Visible publication date on article page.
qualifying_updates.summary: DevOps.com reported that Atlassian is positioning Jira as a control surface for assigning, tracking, reviewing, and governing AI coding-agent work, including connections to Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Codex.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This is upstream-owned product news, but the local practice implication is workflow-state governance: issue trackers can become agent-control planes only if tickets carry acceptance criteria, review ownership, audit evidence, and human approval boundaries.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Route broad product coverage upstream; retain local notes around issue-to-agent handoff contracts, PR review state, governance fields, and auditability of agent-generated work.

qualifying_updates.source_title: Pervaziv AI Unveils AI Model Ensemble in Cortex 5.2 for Secure, Private AI-Assisted Software Development
qualifying_updates.date_basis: Visible publication date on press release page.
qualifying_updates.summary: Pervaziv AI announced Cortex 5.2 and a model ensemble for private AI-assisted software development, describing layered on-device privacy, prompt-injection defense, security analysis, safety-aware decisions, and coding assistance.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The product and vendor are upstream-owned, but the local practice signal is that private coding-agent deployments increasingly bundle privacy locality, security review, prompt-injection defense, and model specialization as one operating boundary.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Keep the local note at the pattern level: private agent harnesses should document data locality, specialized model routing, prompt-injection controls, and security-review evidence.

qualifying_updates.source_title: How Presidio's ISO/IEC 42001 Certification Sets a New Standard in AI Governance
qualifying_updates.date_basis: Visible publication date on analysis page; source says Presidio announced certification on July 15, 2026.
qualifying_updates.summary: Futurum reported Presidio's ISO/IEC 42001 certification and framed AI management-system certification as a procurement trust signal for enterprise AI services.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: For AI-assisted development adoption, partner or platform selection may need evidence beyond feature lists: documented AI management systems, governance controls, compliance proof, and auditable operating practices can become vendor-selection criteria.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Potential ingest belongs under adoption and governance: procurement checklists for AI-assisted development vendors should ask for verifiable AI governance credentials and operating evidence.

qualifying_updates.date_basis: Visible publication date on source page.

The page explicitly warns that its summaries are AI-generated and should be verified against originals.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This is a weak secondary pointer, but it matches local context-selection practice: agents should classify task scope before broad repository reading and should report when evidence comes from a simulator or secondary summary.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Follow-up should verify the linked preprint before synthesis; if it qualifies, map it to context-selection and agent-loop cost controls rather than broad model coverage.
